title: The History of Halo | Combat Evolved to Campaign Evolved | Gaming History
description: The full history of Halo: Bungie, the original Xbox launch, Halo 2 and 3, 343 Industries, the Master Chief Collection, Halo Infinite, Halo Studios and Campaign Evolved.

sections.heading: Finish the fight
sections.script: A lone supersoldier in green armor, a ring shaped world in the sky and a theme that gives you goosebumps. Halo is the series that defined shooters on consoles and made Xbox a household name. In this video we walk through the history of Halo: from the launch of the original Xbox in two thousand one, through the golden years of Halo Two and Halo Three, to the studio changes, the free to play Halo Infinite and the new Halo Studios era. We will look at the dates, the sales milestones and the people behind the games, and we will end with the newest chapter, the return of Combat Evolved on more platforms than ever before. Whether you have played since day one or you are new to Halo, welcome. Let's finish the fight.

sections.heading: Bungie and the Xbox launch
sections.script: The story begins with a small studio called Bungie. In June two thousand, Microsoft announced that it was acquiring Bungie, which gave the company the rights to its upcoming shooter. On November fifteenth, two thousand one, the original Xbox launched in North America, and Halo: Combat Evolved launched with it. The game starred Master Chief, a cybernetically enhanced supersoldier, and it was developed by Bungie and published by Microsoft. It quickly became the reason to own the console. Microsoft announced in April two thousand two that the game had passed one million copies in record time for a game on a console of that generation. Many fans say that without Halo, the Xbox might never have survived its first years, and the game's music, vehicles and large open battlefields set a style that other shooters copied for years.

sections.heading: Halo 2 and online console gaming
sections.script: Three years later, Halo Two arrived on November ninth, two thousand four, and it became a cultural event. Microsoft said the game earned one hundred and twenty five million dollars in sales in its first twenty four hours in the United States and Canada, with about two point four million copies sold. Players lined up at midnight to buy it. The big revolution was online play. Through Xbox Live, players could jump into multiplayer matches against opponents around the world, and the game became a standard for how console shooters handle online games. Its success proved that online play could be at the heart of a console game. The campaign also ended on a famous cliffhanger that kept fans talking for years.

sections.heading: Halo 3 and the peak
sections.script: Halo Three was released for Xbox 360 on September twenty fifth, two thousand seven. Microsoft estimated that it earned one hundred and seventy million dollars in the United States alone during its first twenty four hours, one of the biggest entertainment launches ever at that point. It wrapped up the story of Master Chief and the war against the Covenant, and it added fan favorite features such as the Forge map editor and saved gameplay films, so players could build and share their own creations. Just days after launch, in October two thousand seven, Microsoft announced that Bungie would become an independent company. Bungie went on to make two more Halo games, ending with Halo: Reach, and then stepped away from the series.

sections.heading: 343 Industries takes over
sections.script: With Bungie gone, Microsoft needed a new home for Halo. The answer was 343 Industries, a studio created inside Microsoft and named after the character 343 Guilty Spark. It took full control of the franchise in two thousand twelve and released Halo Four that year, starting a new story arc for Master Chief with the help of his AI companion Cortana. A few years later came Halo Five: Guardians, released on October twenty seventh, twenty fifteen, for Xbox One. The new studio had a tough job. It had to respect what Bungie had built while giving the series a new direction, and fans debated almost every decision. That debate shows how much Halo mattered to people.

sections.heading: The Master Chief Collection
sections.script: In November two thousand fourteen, 343 Industries released Halo: The Master Chief Collection on Xbox One, bringing the main Halo games together in one package with improved visuals. It should have been a celebration, but the launch was rough. On November eleventh, players struggled to get into multiplayer matches, and the studio apologized within days. Studio head Bonnie Ross later published a longer apology, and the team kept patching the game for a long time. The story has a happy ending. The collection was fixed, expanded, and later arrived on PC in the following years, where a new generation of players could finally enjoy the older games in good shape. It is a classic example of a rocky launch followed by a long recovery, and a reminder that studios can win players back by listening and fixing problems.

sections.heading: Halo Infinite
sections.script: Halo Infinite was first announced in two thousand eighteen, and it finally launched in late twenty twenty one after a long wait. The free to play multiplayer arrived first, on November fifteenth, twenty twenty one, exactly on the twentieth anniversary of the franchise. The campaign followed on December eighth. It was a big change for the series, because for the first time the multiplayer part was free for everyone. The strategy worked. In January twenty twenty two, Microsoft's chief executive said that Halo Infinite had passed twenty million players, the biggest launch in the history of the series. Fans praised the controls and the feel of the shooting, and the game gave the community a fresh start after years of waiting.

sections.heading: A franchise bigger than games
sections.script: By twenty twenty one, Halo had sold more than eighty one million copies, according to reports around its twentieth anniversary, and its total franchise revenue, including books, toys and other products, was reported at around six billion dollars. The story also reached television. The Halo series premiered on Paramount Plus on March twenty fourth, twenty twenty two, with Pablo Schreiber starring as Master Chief. The show gave the characters a new audience and sparked plenty of debate among longtime fans. Halo has also been the subject of novels, comics, animated films and a huge esports scene that has hosted its own world championship. The universe has grown far beyond the first game.

sections.heading: Halo Studios and Unreal Engine
sections.script: In October two thousand twenty four, at the Halo World Championship, 343 Industries announced that it was changing its name to Halo Studios. At the same time, the team revealed that future Halo games would move away from the in house Slipspace engine and use Unreal Engine Five. The studio said the aim was to let developers focus on making games instead of building tools, and that multiple new Halo projects were in development. Studio head Pierre Hintze said the goal was to change the way Halo games are made. It was a big shift, and it set up the next chapter for the series, with a faster pace and new technology behind the scenes.

sections.heading: Campaign Evolved and your Halo
sections.script: That brings us to the newest chapter. Halo: Campaign Evolved, a full remake of the original Combat Evolved campaign, was released on July twenty eighth, twenty twenty six, on Windows PC, Xbox Series X and S, and for the first time on PlayStation 5. It marks the biggest change in how Halo reaches players. From a single Xbox launch title in two thousand one to a franchise on every major platform, Halo has come a very long way. Now it is your turn. Which Halo game is your favorite, and what is your best multiplayer memory? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history. Thanks for watching, Spartan.
